Akananuru 242 names the remedy and its deadline, 'மறிஉயிர் வழங்கா அளவை ... முயங்கல் இயைவன்', while 273 ends on 'நெஞ்சு நடுக்குறூஉம்'. The different treatment is real.

The verbal echo is real: 'உள்ளுபு மறந்தறியேமே' against 'உள்ளுவன் மன்யான் மறப்பின் மறப்பறியேன்'. But in Ainkurunuru 298 the man speaks with no friend present, against 'அருளாள் ஆயினும்', so 'both doubts the friend tests him with' is not in the poem. Neither verse limits the other.

Kuruntokai 183 gives the likeness as the poet's own comparison, 'காயாப் பூக்கெழு பெருஞ்சினை மென்மயில் எருத்தில் தோன்றும்'. Thinaimalai 107 makes it a fear inside the scene, 'கருவுற்ற காயாக் கணமயிலென்று அஞ்சி ... பூங்கோடல்'. The move from simile to an error made within the landscape is specific and accurate.

The lizard omen is shared ('பகுவாய்ப் பல்லி படுதொறும் பரவி', 'பாங்கத்துப் பல்லி படும்'), and one poem is his imagining while the other is her own reading. But the omen is a common topic, and nothing in either poem shows each lover expecting the other to be reading it, so the 'shared language' claim is not in the Tamil.

The formula is shared ('வேப்புநனை யன்ன நெடுங்கள் களவன் ... மண்அளை', 'வேப்புநனை அன்ன நெடுங்கண் நீர்ஞெண்டு ... மண்அளை'). But in Ainkurunuru 30 it is the paddy's flowers that drop into the hole ('மண்அளை நிறைய நெல்லின் இரும்பூ உறைக்கும்'). The crab does nothing, so the 'hoarding' act on which the teaches rests is misread.

poems.note: The bull scenes are joined by open markers (ஒத்தன) to warriors and clouds, not to the lovers.
The creature that loses its mate to the tiger suffers rather than acts, and line 2 is obscure.

iraicchi.act: the peacock dances with its mate in the morning sun on his own hill
iraicchi.sense: the man whose land keeps its pairs together has gone away and left her, and should stay with her as his peacock stays with its mate

iraicchi.act: the elephant eats the hill rice and sleeps safe in the cool shade of the maraam grove
iraicchi.sense: those joined to the hill man rest as secure as his elephant sleeps (ஏமாப்பு)

ullurai.anchor: ஞெகிழ் தோள் கலுழ்ந்த கண்ணர் மலர் தீய்ந்தனையர் நின் நயந்தோரே

poems.note: The vehicle is the old boat used for years, worn by the waves and laid aside without incense. It stands for the women he used, who are wasted and then dropped. The speaker is the courtesan, who may use it freely.
The birds hurrying to their young are the whole poem, so striking them leaves nothing, and the separation is not stated in the poem or its thurai.

The bard's wife gives little fish for much paddy. This matches the bard, who gives little (lies) and takes much (women's beauty). It has two pairs, though one rests on the matched words பாண்மகள் / பாண்மகன்.

ullurai.anchor: உற்றோர் மறவா நோய்தந்து கண்டோர் தண்டா நலங்கொண் டனனே

poems.note: The young monkey leaps away and the bamboo springs up like a rod jerking a fish from the pool. This matches him leaving her and having taken her beauty.
The cloud raining at the hill man's shout matches her weeping only by look, not by an act.
The makanril pair is joined to the lovers by போல, so it is an open simile. It is not tagged as iraicchi either, since the sense is stated.
The colophon thinai is vaakai (puram), so both fields are null although the passage describes the queen's grief.
